cards.front: What "the model" you deploy really is
cards.back: The weights file plus the architecture config and the tokenizer, loaded by a runtime such as vLLM or llama.cpp. All three must match.

Open-weight means you can download the weights under some licence. The OSI definition also requires the training code and enough data detail to rebuild the model, so most "open" models are only open-weight.
Monthly active users, using outputs to train other models, or attribution. Read the licence on the exact checkpoint and record it in your model registry.
Base is pre-trained only and just continues text. Instruct adds instruction tuning and preference training, and is the default download for apps.
A small add-on file, often under 1% of the model. Runtimes like vLLM can load many adapters on one base model, so ten fine-tuned tasks cost one GPU.
params_B × bytes per param: BF16 2, FP8/INT8 1, 4-bit about 0.55. Then total ≈ weights × 1.1 + KV cache + about 1 GB.
Llama 3.1 8B keeps about 128 KB per token, so 32 users at 32k context need about 137 GB of cache, eight times the 16 GB of weights.

Memory follows total parameters, speed follows active ones. gpt-oss-120b has about 117B parameters, routes each token through about 5B, and fits one 80 GB GPU only because it ships in 4-bit (about 63 GB).
tokens/month ≈ GPU cost per month ÷ API price per token. One ~$2/h GPU (≈$1,460/month) at $0.60 per 1M tokens breaks even near 2.4B tokens a month.
Small retrieval-pipeline models: embedders, cross-encoder rerankers, classifiers and routers. Owning the embedder also means your index vectors never change because a provider retired a version.
Load .safetensors rather than pickled files, never set trust_remote_code on an unreviewed repo, and pin, mirror and checksum the exact revision you evaluated.

quiz.q: A team sized GPUs for the weights only. Users and context grew, and requests now queue or run out of memory. What did they miss?
quiz.why: The KV cache often dominates; budget it from context length and concurrency.

quiz.q: Data must never leave the network and the system runs air-gapped. Which route works?
choices: Any of them with a private region
quiz.why: Only self-hosting runs with no internet at run time.

quiz.q: An MoE model was sized by its active parameters and won't load. Why?
choices: Every expert must be loaded, so memory follows total parameters
Active parameters ignore the KV cache only
quiz.why: MoE saves compute per token, not memory.

quiz.q: A self-hosted model rambles, confuses roles and ignores the system prompt. Most likely cause?
quiz.why: Use the tokenizer's own chat template.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid loading pickled .bin or .pt weights from strangers?
One model size is Apache-2.0. What can you assume about the other sizes from the same vendor?
choices: They are all OSI open source
quiz.why: One vendor can ship different sizes under different terms.

quiz.q: Volume is low and spiky with no GPU team. Which route usually wins on cost?
choices: Per-token pricing via a closed API or hosted open-weight
quiz.why: Idle GPUs still cost, so below the break-even per-token pricing wins.
